title: Left extension of an encoded block
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over a finite alphabet $\Gamma$, let $q$ be one of its states, and let $x$ be a word over the simulator alphabet. For any valid input-head position $p$, output word, integer frontier $z$, and finite zipper stacks $l,r$, running the simulator for exactly $k$ steps from the backward-facing configuration in the left-extension phase with counter $0$ yields the backward-facing configuration in that phase with counter $k$, frontier $z-k$, left stack equal to the encoded unmarked blank block prepended to $l$, and right stack obtained by dropping the first $k$ entries of $r$; the input-head position and output word are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: Finite machine $M$ with finite state set and decidable equality
replaced:
For the single-tape simulator of a machine $M$ with $k$ work tapes and any source state
$q$: from any backward-facing zipper configuration whose control is in the
left-extension phase carrying $q$ with counter $0$, running exactly $k$ transitions
writes the encoded unmarked blank block in reversed cell order while moving left, ending
in the left-extension phase with counter $k$ and the work head moved left by $k$ cells;
the input head and output are unchanged.
